text: #913, step 3 of #789's plan, P-0913, recorded for #932, which finished the factory's build by hand. A replay's harness runs in the same process as the driver it runs, for TypeScript and for ordinary Python alike, so a driver that reaches into the harness can have it seal records of code that never ran. As D-0183 says of the existing Python collector, that is tampering with the gate, and nothing inside that process can prevent it. The seal guards against records written, changed or replayed outside the harness. Nor can the harness tell a binding to a stand-in, or a read that makes state up, from a real one. Against a driver that does any of this, the check is review: the driver's writer is told never to reach into the harness, and its reviewer is told to report code that does and to inspect every binding and read-back. The factory posts that review with the pull request as an opinion, and doesn't wait on it before it merges a modeled project's code (D-0082). The second agent's review of the build asked for completion to be kept out of the driver's reach. This turns that down, so it is proposed for @gitdek. Running the driver in a process the harness doesn't share wouldn't close it either, since the harness would still call the application and read its state through the driver's code, and nothing that would close it is decided here.
